title: token-level-observability-cost-latency-breakdown-and-alert-tuning
author: Aisha Patel
description: Context: customers and internal product teams asked for token-level cost and latency breakdowns, better token instrumentation, and tuned alert thresholds after a recent production incident where background batching caused high tail latency. This PR adds token-level metrics for cost attribution and latency, wiring them into existing dashboards and implementing a small alert tuning pass to reduce noise while protecting user-facing SLOs. Motivation: enable precise cost accounting by token category (prompt/system/response/embedding), improve observability for tail-latency debugging, and reduce pager fatigue by moving low-signal alerts to warning channels and tightening critical SLO alerts. Changes: 1) New metrics: redwood.tokens.count_by_category, redwood.tokens.cost_by_category, redwood.token_latency.p50/p95/p99_by_model_and_category, redwood.kvcache.hit_rate_by_prefix. Metrics include labels: model, route, customer_tier, token_category, quantization_profile. 2) Tracing: add token-affine trace/span tags to the request path so slow-token generation can be correlated with GPU scheduling spans. 3) Logs: enrich generation debug logs with token_category and batch_id when debug is enabled to avoid high-volume logging in prod. 4) Dashboards: new Token Cost & Latency dashboard with per-model and per-route panes, cost heatmap, and top-20 expensive prompt signatures. 5) Alert tuning: adjust existing alert rules: move redwood.high_token_cost from page to slack-warning for non-enterprise customers, set dynamic thresholds for redwood.latency_p99 with lookback-based baselining, and create a new composite alert redwood.token_generation_regression that ties quality eval regressions to token-cost spikes. 6) Backfill tooling: add a small job to compute historical token_cost_by_category for the last 90 days for dashboard backfilling. Checklist: - [x] Instrumentation PR: metrics + traces + logs - [x] Dashboard JSONs exported and validated - [x] Alert rules updated and run through simulated firing test - [x] Backfill job added and dry-run validated - [x] Added unit tests for metric tagging and integration test for alert simulation Related: ENG-1423 for token-costing initiative, SUP-987 incident postmortem. Rollout plan: feature-gated metrics (env var OBS_TOKEN_LEVEL=true) to enable gradual rollout to staging then canary then prod. Monitoring: dashboards available in Grafana/Metriq, alert changes will start in staging and promoted to prod after 48h of stability. Notes: kept the perf overhead minimal by sampling token-level traces at 1% by default and enabling full traces only for canary runs. No breaking API changes.

review_thread: Miguel Rivera: Can we avoid adding cardinality by including customer_id directly? Suggest using customer_tier instead.
Aisha Patel: Agreed, switched to customer_tier label to keep cardinality bounded. Full audit in code comment.
Emma Zhou: The p99 calculation looks good but can we use a 5m sliding window instead of 1m to reduce flapping?
Aisha Patel: Updated alert rule to use 5m window and added backoff for noisy routes.
Noah Kim: I ran the alert-sim job and saw one false positive on an internal dev route—added exclusion for dev.* routes.
Aisha Patel: Added route exclude filter and documented in rollout steps.
Emma Zhou: Approved after verifying dashboards render; left minor nit about help text.
